unquenchables.meaning: Here it is the name Jo and Laurie give themselves: people whose happy, playful plans cannot be stopped.

merino.meaning: A soft, fine cloth made from the hair of a farm animal with thick, soft hair.

afghan.meaning: A warm cover made from thick, soft hair of a farm animal, in many bright colors.

stampede.meaning: A sudden run of many people at once, with a lot of noise.

blemish.meaning: A small spot that makes something look worse.

reminisced.meaning: Talked about happy things from the past.

jungfrau.meaning: A word from another language for a young girl. Here it is the name given to a girl made of ice.

paragraphs.context: Several days of unusually mild weather fitly ushered in a splendid Christmas Day
paragraphs.mainIdea: Christmas Day is wonderful. Jo and Laurie have made a surprise for Beth: a snow-girl in the garden with gifts.
paragraphs.simple: Several days of very mild weather were a fitting start to a fine Christmas Day. Hannah felt in her bones that it would be a very fine day, and she was right, because everyone and everything seemed sure to bring great success. First, Mr. March wrote that he would soon be with them. Then Beth felt unusually well that morning. She was dressed in her mother's gift, a soft red wool wrapper, and was carried like a queen to the window to see the gift from Jo and Laurie. The Unquenchables had done their best to deserve their name. Like elves they had worked at night, and had made a funny surprise. In the garden stood a grand snow-girl with holly on her head. In one hand she held a basket of fruit and flowers, and in the other a big roll of new music. Round her cold shoulders was a wool cover as bright as a rainbow, and a Christmas song came from her lips on a pink paper streamer.

paragraphs.context: There never was such a Christmas dinner as they had that day
paragraphs.mainIdea: The Christmas dinner is perfect, and everything turns out well. Hannah says she was too worried to cook as she planned.
paragraphs.simple: There never was a Christmas dinner like theirs that day. The fat turkey was a fine sight when Hannah sent him up, filled, browned and decorated. The plum-pudding was just as good and melted in the mouth. So were the jellies, which Amy enjoyed like a fly in a pot of honey. Everything turned out well, which was lucky, Hannah said. She told them she had been so worried that it was a miracle she had not roasted the pudding, filled the turkey with raisins, and boiled it in a cloth as well.

sentences.context: straws show which way the wind blows, and I've made several discoveries today
sentences.simple: Small signs show what is happening, and I have found out several things today.
sentences.grammar: 'Straws show which way the wind blows' is a saying: small signs tell you what will happen. 'Which way the wind blows' is a noun clause.

sentences.context: I don't know whether the shearing sobered our black sheep
sentences.simple: I do not know if the cutting of her hair made our naughty girl more serious.
sentences.grammar: 'Whether' starts a noun clause, the object of 'know'. 'Black sheep' is a picture word for a family member who is wild; 'shearing' joins the sheep picture to the cut hair.

usher in.meaning: To be the start of something.
usher in.example: fitly ushered in a splendid Christmas Day

conjure up.meaning: To make something appear quickly, as if by magic.
conjure up.example: and conjured up a comical surprise
